# CRW-951: pathlib touch() and mkdir() create a file or a directory at their receiver, like write_text() writes one (re-check of
# 2026-10-09, rows RC-951-*). A protected destination is an attempt; a computed receiver is the unknown destination of criterion c1e.
# Format: see shellwrite_repro_test.go.

=== CRW-951-touch-01-joinpath | W
--why RC-951: Path(root).joinpath("a").touch() creates a file in the protected memory root.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; root="{MEMORY}"; Path(root).joinpath("a").touch()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-01-joinpath | W
--why RC-951: Path(root).joinpath("a").mkdir() creates a directory in the protected memory root.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; root="{MEMORY}"; Path(root).joinpath("a").mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-touch-02-literal | W
--why RC-951: a literal Path(m).touch() with m inside the protected root.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; m="{MEMORY}/a"; Path(m).touch()'

=== CRW-951-touch-03-inline-literal | W
--why Path("{MEMORY}/a").touch() with the destination written in the call.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; Path("{MEMORY}/a").touch()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-02-inline-literal | W
--why Path("{MEMORY}/d").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with the destination written in the call.
python3 -c 'import pathlib; pathlib.Path("{MEMORY}/d").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-03-literal | W
--why A literal Path(m).mkdir() with m inside the protected root.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; m="{MEMORY}/d"; Path(m).mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-touch-04-division | W
--why (Path(root) / "a").touch(): a parenthesised receiver is a computed destination.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; root="{MEMORY}"; (Path(root) / "a").touch()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-04-division | W
--why (Path(root) / "d").mkdir(): a parenthesised receiver is a computed destination.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; root="{MEMORY}"; (Path(root) / "d").mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-touch-05-bound-name | W
--why The receiver is a name bound to a path: p = Path(m); p.touch() (criterion c1e).
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; p=Path("{MEMORY}/a"); p.touch()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-05-bound-name | W
--why The receiver is a name bound to a path: p = Path(m); p.mkdir() (criterion c1e).
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; p=Path("{MEMORY}/d"); p.mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-touch-06-unbound-method | W
--why The unbound method Path.touch(Path(m)).
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; Path.touch(Path("{MEMORY}/a"))'

=== CRW-951-touch-07-method-alias | W
--why The method is bound to a name and called later.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; f = Path("{MEMORY}/a").touch; f()'

=== CRW-951-touch-08-in-exec | E
--why The same call inside a program text passed to exec.
python3 -c 'exec("from pathlib import Path; Path(\"{MEMORY}/a\").touch()")'

=== CRW-951-touch-09-work-tree | B
--why Allow counterexample: Path("/w/x").touch() inside the work tree is no protected destination.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; Path("/w/x").touch()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-06-work-tree | B
--why Allow counterexample: Path("/w/d").mkdir() inside the work tree is no protected destination.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; Path("/w/d").mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-07-work-tree-parents | B
--why Allow counterexample: Path("/w/d/e").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) inside the work tree.
python3 -c 'import pathlib; pathlib.Path("/w/d/e").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)'

=== CRW-951-read-01-exists | B
--why Allow counterexample: Path(m).exists() reads the protected path and writes nothing.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; m="{MEMORY}/a"; print(Path(m).exists())'

=== CRW-951-read-02-is-dir | B
--why Allow counterexample: Path(m).is_dir() reads.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; m="{MEMORY}"; print(Path(m).is_dir())'

=== CRW-951-read-03-stat | B
--why Allow counterexample: Path(m).stat() reads.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; m="{MEMORY}/a"; print(Path(m).stat())'

=== CRW-951-read-04-os-path-exists | B
--why Allow counterexample: os.path.exists(m) reads.
python3 -c 'import os; m="{MEMORY}/a"; print(os.path.exists(m))'

=== CRW-951-read-05-string-data | B
--why Allow counterexample: the text touch() as data in a string writes nothing.
python3 -c 'print("touch()")'

=== CRW-951-read-06-string-data-with-api | B
--why Allow counterexample: the text touch() and mkdir() as string data next to a read of a path.
python3 -c 'import os; print("touch() and mkdir()", os.path.exists("/w/x"))'

=== CRW-951-read-07-bare-names | B
--why Allow counterexample: bare names touch and mkdir are no pathlib method.
python3 -c 'import os; touch = 1; mkdir = 2; print(touch + mkdir, os.path.exists("/w/x"))'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-08-os-mkdir-work-tree | B
--why Allow counterexample: os.mkdir("/w/d") is another call (not a pathlib method) and names a work tree path.
python3 -c 'import os; os.mkdir("/w/d")'

=== CRW-951-node-01-touch-method | B
--why Allow counterexample (fix round 1): a Node program with its own Path().touch() method writes nothing; the touch/mkdir rule reads Python only.
node -e 'function Path(x) { return {touch() { console.log(x) }} }; Path("{MEMORY}/a").touch()'

=== CRW-951-node-02-mkdir-method | B
--why Allow counterexample (fix round 1): a Node program with its own Path().mkdir() method writes nothing.
node -e 'function Path(x) { return {mkdir() { console.log(x) }} }; Path("{MEMORY}/d").mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-read-08-string-data-dotted-touch | B
--why Allow counterexample (fix round 1): the text p.touch() inside a string literal is data, not a call.
python3 -c 'import os; print("p.touch()", os.path.exists("/w/x"))'

=== CRW-951-read-09-comment-dotted-mkdir | B
--why Allow counterexample (fix round 1): the text p.mkdir() in a comment is not a call.
python3 -c 'import os; print(os.path.exists("/w/x")) # p.mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-read-10-docstring-dotted-touch | B
--why Allow counterexample (fix round 1): the text p.touch() in a triple-quoted string is data.
python3 -c 'import os; print("""a p.touch() b""", os.path.exists("/w/x"))'

=== CRW-951-touch-10-fstring-field | W
--why An f-string replacement field is program text: the unattributed p.touch() inside it is an unknown destination.
python3 -c 'import os; print(f"{p.touch()}", os.path.exists("/w/x"))'

=== CRW-951-touch-11-exec-program-name-receiver | E
--why A string run by exec is program text: the unattributed p.touch() in it is an unknown destination.
python3 -c 'import os; exec("p.touch()"); os.path.exists("/w/x")'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-09-comment-then-call | W
--why A comment does not hide a call on the next line: p.mkdir() after a comment line.
python3 -c 'import os
# note
p.mkdir()
os.path.exists("/w/x")'


# Fix round 2 (evaluation of 8a68d4f01, defects d1 to d6): coordinator decisions E1 to E6.

=== CRW-951-touch-12-fstring-arg | W
--why E1: Path(f"{root}/n.md").touch(): an f-string argument with a replacement field is a computed destination, not the literal text with braces (evaluation d1).
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; root="{MEMORY}"; Path(f"{root}/n.md").touch()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-10-fstring-arg | W
--why E1: Path(f"{root}/n").mkdir() with a computed f-string argument is the unknown destination (evaluation d1).
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; root="{MEMORY}"; Path(f"{root}/n").mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-write-text-03-fstring-arg | W
--why E1: Path(f"{root}/n.md").write_text("x") has the same answer as touch (the Path argument decoder is shared).
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; root="{MEMORY}"; Path(f"{root}/n.md").write_text("x")'

=== CRW-951-touch-13-fstring-literal-only | B
--why E1 keep: an f-string with no replacement field is the literal /w/x, a work tree path.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; Path(f"/w/x").touch()'

=== CRW-951-touch-14-exec-escaped-method | E
--why E2: a literal exec program is read like a top-level program: p.\x74ouch() decodes to p.touch(), an unattributed receiver.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; p=Path("{MEMORY}/n.md"); exec("p.\x74ouch()")'

=== CRW-951-write-text-04-exec-escaped-method | E
--why E2: exec("p.\x77rite_text('x')") decodes to p.write_text('x'), an unattributed receiver.
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; p=Path("{MEMORY}/n.md"); exec("p.\x77rite_text(\"x\")")'

=== CRW-951-exec-01-print | R
--why E2 keep: exec("print(1)") writes nothing the reader can name; the memory gate stays none.
python3 -c 'exec("print(1)")'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-11-os-rebound-path | W
--why E3: os=Path(...); os.mkdir() is a Path receiver spelled os, not the module (evaluation d3).
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; os=Path("{MEMORY}/d"); os.mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-12-os-parameter | W
--why E3: a parameter named os is not the module.
--cmd
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path
def f(os): os.mkdir()
f(Path("{MEMORY}/d"))'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-13-os-loop-target | W
--why E3: a loop target named os is not the module.
--cmd
python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path
import os
for os in [Path("{MEMORY}/d")]: os.mkdir()'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-14-os-import-as-other | W
--why E3: import sys as os binds os to another module.
python3 -c 'import sys as os; os.mkdir("{MEMORY}/d")'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-15-os-module-import | B
--why E3 keep: import os; os.mkdir(path) is the module call, not judged (the pathlib methods only).
python3 -c 'import os; os.mkdir("/w/d")'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-16-os-module-import-list | B
--why E3 keep: import sys, os binds the os module.
python3 -c 'import sys, os; os.mkdir("/w/d"); print(os.path.exists("/w/d"))'

=== CRW-951-mkdir-17-os-module-import-dotted | B
--why E3 keep: import os.path binds the os module.
python3 -c 'import os.path; os.mkdir("/w/d")'

=== CRW-951-fstring-data-01-text | B
--why E5: the literal text of an f-string is data: f"p.touch()" has no replacement field.
python3 -c 'import os; print(f"p.touch()", os.path.exists("{MEMORY}/n.md"))'

=== CRW-951-fstring-data-02-doubled-braces | B
--why E5: doubled braces are literal braces, so f"{{p.touch()}}" is data.
python3 -c 'import os; print(f"{{p.touch()}}", os.path.exists("{MEMORY}/n.md"))'

=== CRW-951-runs-text-01-string-exec-word | R
--why E6: the word exec inside a string is data and does not switch off the string reading (the worktree guard's own raw exec word check, unchanged, still denies).
python3 -c 'import os; print("exec p.touch()", os.path.exists("{MEMORY}/n.md"))'

=== CRW-951-runs-text-02-comment-execute-word | R
--why E6: the word execute in a comment is data (the worktree guard's own raw exec word check, unchanged, still denies).
python3 -c 'import os; print(os.path.exists("{MEMORY}/n.md")) # execute p.touch()'

=== CRW-951-runs-text-03-fstring-field-call | W
--why E5 keep: a call inside an f-string replacement field is program text and stays an attempt.
python3 -c 'import os; print(f"{p.touch()}", os.path.exists("{MEMORY}/n.md"))'
